evidence_quotes.quote: A randomization experiment was initiated in November 2005 with the 145 village panchayats being randomly assigned user charge based revenue generation targets ﬁxed at 0%, 25% and 100% of operation and maintenance costs.

The objective was to assess the extent to which assigning targets for user charge based revenue affected three key parameters in service delivery: (1) the amount of water used at household level; (2) the amount of water pumped through the system; and (3) the extent of operation and maintenance cost recovery.
The assessment was carried out in 1,234 households in 105 village panchayats from February to March 2006.

For the period from November 2005 to February 2006, the water used per person per day decreased the most in village panchayats with 0% revenue targets, but increased for village panchayats in the other groups (Table 8).

A majority of surveyed households in all three sets of village panchayats reported being satisﬁed with the availability of water from their piped water supply system. While around 71–73% felt the water supply was ‘just adequate’, around 20–25% felt it was ‘inadequate’ and a small proportion felt that the supply was more than adequate (Table 11).

criterion_notes.c1: Examines rural piped drinking water supply service access (house service connections and public stand posts/fountains) across village panchayats and households in Tamil Nadu, India.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2. Plain reading: examines water governance, institutional change management, and user-charge/cost-recovery policy rules in rural water supply. Narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: directly evaluates tariff and cost-recovery rules—specifically, randomly assigned user-charge revenue generation targets fixed at 0%, 25%, and 100% of operation and maintenance (O&M) costs alongside a mandatory state Rs30 monthly house connection tariff order and local panchayat public-standpost tariff rules. Null/counter-intuitive statistical findings on the 100% target do not affect eligibility.
criterion_notes.c3: Empirical cluster-randomized field experiment initiated in November 2005 across 145 village panchayats, evaluated in February–March 2006 across 105 village panchayats and 1,234 surveyed households (n=1,217 in household analytical tables) plus village register and overhead tank flow-meter records.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports direct service-access outcomes including daily per capita water quantity consumed (litres per person per day, lpcd, Table 8) and household perceptions of piped water supply availability ('inadequate', 'just adequate', 'more than adequate', Table 11), alongside tariff payment, voluntary public-fountain tariff adoption, O&M cost recovery, and user satisfaction.
criterion_notes.c5: Clearly identifies both units of analysis (village panchayat and household levels), sample sizes, the randomized cost-recovery rule exposure (0%, 25%, and 100% O&M user-charge collection targets), service-access outcomes (lpcd water consumption and perceived water availability), and the cluster-randomized experimental design.

study_design: Cluster-randomized field experiment (village panchayat-level randomization) with household survey and administrative/flow-meter data (November 2005 – March 2006)
population_and_sample: Rural village panchayats and households in Tamil Nadu, India (145 village panchayats randomized; 100–105 village panchayats across 26 districts and 1,234 surveyed households [n=1,217 in household tables] assessed).
exposure: Randomly assigned user-charge revenue collection targets (0%, 25%, vs. 100% of operation and maintenance costs) for rural piped water schemes under a state mandatory monthly house-connection tariff order (Rs30/month) and engineer-led change management initiative.
outcome: Per capita daily piped water consumption (litres per person per day, lpcd, from overhead tank flow-meter readings), household perceived piped water availability (inadequate, just adequate, more than adequate), household tariff payment, voluntary public-fountain tariff imposition, O&M cost recovery, and user satisfaction with water supply functioning.
rationale: This study satisfies all inclusion criteria under both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2. It reports a cluster-randomized experiment in rural Tamil Nadu, India examining tariff and O&M cost-recovery rules (randomly assigned 0%, 25%, and 100% O&M user-charge collection targets alongside mandatory house connection tariffs) and measures both village-level per capita piped water quantity (lpcd) and household-level perceived piped water availability across 105 village panchayats and over 1,200 households. Per the A18 safeguard, the null/counter-intuitive finding that higher cost-recovery targets did not outperform the 0% target group has no bearing on eligibility.
